summaryEn: Teaches you the language of a recipe: the passive says what is done, not who does it.
Teaches you to order politely and to ask for the bill, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to choose between two products by comparing them and to give your reasons.
Teaches you to discuss what to bring and to pay a compliment in a subordinate clause.
Teaches you to describe a dish with a relative clause, whose pronoun changes case as the object.
Teaches you to say the order is wrong without a row, and to give your reason in a clause of reason.
Teaches you to state an intention and a purpose with an infinitive phrase: what you plan to do.
Teaches you to compare the table manners of two countries with paired conjunctions.
Teaches you to describe jobs in time order: before, during and after.
Teaches you to thank your host and to leave politely, with fixed-preposition verbs.
Teaches you to compare two sellers and to back your choice with figures.
Teaches you to return an item and to give your reason in a clause of reason.
Teaches you to ask about bank details you do not know, with indirect question patterns.
Teaches you to describe a past transaction with the past form of the passive.
Teaches you to decline adjectives correctly in front of the noun, talking size and fabric.
Teaches you to say what an object is made of, with a relative clause after a preposition.
Teaches you to discuss the economy in a balanced way, with paired conjunctions.
Teaches you to describe a table in passive sentences and to interpret a figure.
Teaches you to describe an advert with relative clauses and to ask about the details.
Teaches you the polite but firm language of a written complaint, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to ask at the station about details you do not know, with indirect questions.
Teaches you to describe what happened on a flight with the past form of the passive.
Teaches you to say what will be done on the road, with conditional clauses.
Teaches you to understand and to explain the rules in passive sentences.
Teaches you to compare two places to stay and to defend your choice.
Teaches you to describe a place with relative clauses that follow a preposition.
Teaches you to describe a one-off event in the past, with the conjunction als.
Teaches you to tell your own past in the tense that written German uses.
Teaches you to suggest politely what should be done, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to pull the earlier event back in time: two layers of the past.
Teaches you to describe where the pain is, with fixed-preposition verbs.
Teaches you to describe the steps of first aid in passive sentences.
Teaches you to say how a result is reached, with an infinitive phrase and a clause of means.
Teaches you to state an expectation and a worry in a subordinate clause.
Teaches you to describe relatives with dative relative clauses.
Teaches you to describe a one-off past event with the conjunction als.
Teaches you to state the aim of an arrangement with a damit clause.
Teaches you to compare ways of living and to say which you would choose.
Teaches you to describe politely what you want, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to raise a difficult subject with a reservation, using the conjunction obwohl.
Teaches you to understand and to explain the steps of an installation in passive sentences.
Teaches you to explain the cause of a fault in a weil clause.
Teaches you to ask about technical details you do not know, with indirect questions.
Teaches you the most polite way to ask a neighbour for something, in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to state the aim of an arrangement with a damit clause.
Teaches you to report formally what happened, with the past form of the passive.
Teaches you to describe an image with relative clauses.
Teaches you to compare old technology with new.
Teaches you to state an intention and to give advice with an infinitive phrase.
Teaches you to weigh both sides of technology with paired conjunctions.
